thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - multiple nodes in eu-west-1a reporting KubeletRestart and transitioning NotReady. Inference pool 'infer-eu-west' showing pod evictions and increased 5xx rate. Alert group: infra-kubelet-pulse.

maya: seeing 504s on prod inference, customers spiking errors. getting pages now. any recent cluster changes?

jordan: no config pushes from infra in last 3 hours. last deploy was a model rollout at 16:22 which was stable. kubelet logs show repeated 'node not ready: container runtime not responding' + rapid kubelet restarts.

liam: confirmed on dashboards: node count in pool dropped from 12 -> 7 over 6m due to NotReady, HPA didn't kick because pods are daemonset pinned. We have eviction churn causing routing thrash to fallback model, but fallback is saturated.

maya: ok that's customer-impacting. assigning page to @oncall-sre. Jordan, can you grab kubelet logs and paste a snippet?

jordan: pasted: ```
May  5 17:14:33 node-az1 kubelet[1234]: E0517 17:14:33 server.go:123] failed to get cgroup stats: kubernetes.io/kubelet: error reading from /sys/fs/cgroup: input/output error
May  5 17:14:34 node-az1 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=139
May  5 17:14:34 node-az1 kernel: NMI: CPU stuck - killing task kubelet
```

alex: that looks like kernel-level OOM/watchdog causing kubelet crash. we've seen this pattern when GPU driver flaps and triggers GPU oom. Are the nodes running newer driver 525.85?

liam: yes they were on 525.85 from last infra image push. I'd like to cordon the failing nodes to stop scheduling and let autoscaler replace them.

maya: agree. plan: 1) cordon and drain NotReady nodes from infer-eu-west 2) scale up fallback pool in us-east as short-term capacity 3) enable model-routing fallback at edge to route lower-latency customers to dedicated fallback 4) open SEV bridge notes for customers.

chris: on it, cordoning nodes: ```
kubectl cordon node-az1
kubectl drain node-az1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
(reacted with :white_check_mark:)

infra-sre: quick note: when kubelet segfaults like that, first step is check nvdec/nvidia kernel driver logs. can someone collect dmesg + nvidia-smi output before reboot?

jordan: grabbing dmesg and nv logs now. pasting top anomalies: ```
[ 3456.789012] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 3456.789015] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x24:0xffff)
```

maya: confirms GPU driver crash. mitigation: reboot affected nodes after we drain, then pin them to older driver image (524.*) via node maintenance label until we patch.

liam: I'm creating a temporary node-pool with older driver image and adding a taint? prefer: create new nodepool 'infer-eu-west-legacy-driver' with image 524.83 and set nodeSelector for inference pool to allow fallback scheduling.

alex: I'll trigger the nodepool create now and increase replica count. ```
gcloud compute node-groups create infer-eu-west-legacy-driver --image-family infer-24-driver-524 --size 6 --region eu-west-1
```

deploy-bot: rollout started for route policy 'edge-fallback' -> canary 20% (controlled).

support-bot: creating incident ticket INC-2023-8475, tagging impacted customers with high qps above 1k/min. Drafting status update.

maya: Jordan, Chris, monitor for any additional kernel OOM messages. Also enable temporary autoscaler override to add +4 nodes to the fallback pool.

jordan: saw another node segfault; cordoned and drained, then rebooted. After reboot kubelet came back but GPU driver crash log persisted. Forcing node into maintenance 

chris: added node label maintenance=true and tainted: ```
kubectl label node node-az2 maintenance=true
kubectl taint nodes node-az2 maintenance=true:NoSchedule
```
(reacted with :eyes:)

liam: new nodepool 6 nodes ready, I'm patching daemonset tolerations to allow scheduling: ```
kubectl patch daemonset infer-runtime -n prod --patch '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"tolerations": [{"key":"legacy-driver","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'```

alex: routing now shifted ~35% traffic to us-east fallback, latency holding ~220ms for most requests, 504s down 72%.

maya: good. inform SEV channel and draft customer note: "We observed node-level kubelet restarts in eu-west due to GPU driver instability causing transient 5xx on inference requests. We have cordoned affected nodes, provisioned a legacy-driver node pool, and shifted traffic to fallback. Working on a permanent driver rollback and deeper forensic logs."

support-bot: customer bulletin queued to send to impacted customers in 10m.

infra-sre: next steps: capture full crash dumps from affected nodes, escalate to kernel/driver vendor with dmesg + gpu vmcore. Also prepare image patch and test on staging before mass rollout.

jordan: uploading crash logs to internal bucket gs://redwood-infra/incidents/1754003210/gpu-crash-archive.tar.gz

chris: started a rolling reboot of remaining nodes in that AZ one-by-one with a 5m pause between reboots to avoid mass kubelet churn. Using: ```
for n in node-az*; do kubectl cordon $n && kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data && gcloud compute instances reset $n && sleep 300; done
```

maya: handoff to night shift in 2h; create a short runbook in the incident ticket with steps performed and outstanding actions: - rotate drivers - run soak on staging - revert node images - confirm autoscaler thresholds - customer followups.

liam: added runbook note to INC-2023-8475. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

maya: thanks all. I'll stay on bridge until traffic is stable for 30m and then demote to watch. If new spikes happen, escalate to SEV2.

deploy-bot: edge-fallback canary increased to 50% per manual override by maya.

alex: monitoring shows 5xx now ~1.2% (from 7.8%), CPU on fallback nodes up but within limits. Keeping autoscaler +4 for another 45m.

support-bot: initial customer note sent. Will update when we confirm driver rollback plan.

maya: closing the active paging. leaving this thread open for followups and for night shift handoff.

chris: tagging infra-sre for postmortem: need to capture upgrade gating to prevent auto-push of 525.* driver to prod until verified.

infra-sre: acknowledged. scheduling P0 postmortem and driver gating change.
